rule.SIGHT.title: It can see.
rule.SIGHT.hint: Stand in light and it notices you, even through rock. Darkness hides you.
rule.HEARING.title: It can hear.
rule.HEARING.hint: Running, thrown stones and machinery draw it to the sound. Moss muffles footsteps.
rule.SMELL.title: It can smell.
rule.SMELL.hint: It always drifts toward you. Its sniffing grows louder as it gets close.
rule.CONSUME.title: It consumes all.
rule.CONSUME.hint: It has grown through the whole mountain. Tentacles in the walls pin anyone who stands too close: hammer E to tear free. Knots of its flesh on the floor tell it exactly where you are.
rule.ECHO.title: It travels through echoes.
rule.ECHO.hint: Loud noises pull it there instantly. Use stones to send it away.
rule.HASTE.title: It grows restless.
rule.HASTE.hint: It moves a little faster for every minute you spend down here.
rule.BATTERY.title: Your lantern drains fast.
rule.BATTERY.hint: This shift the lantern eats its charge several times faster. Pick up spare cells and switch it off when you can.
rule.COLD.title: You can freeze.
rule.COLD.hint: Darkness chills you. Stay near light or a heater to warm up.
rule.HUNGER.title: You can starve.
rule.HUNGER.hint: Eat canned food to keep going. Hunger slowly slows you down.
shift.label: Shift {0}
shift.1.intro: Midnight. The day crew went down into Pit 9 this morning and no one has come back up. The radio is all static, except now and then a steady knocking, as if someone were tapping on the rock from the other side. The lift has no power. Find the fuses, fill the boxes, ride up. Do not linger.
shift.2.intro: The second night. Nobody mentions the day crew any more, as if they had never existed. Down here the rock carries sound a long way, and last night something heard you. Tread softly.
shift.3.intro: A few rooms still have their heaters burning, though no one works there. The old gatekeeper says the miners used to keep the lamps lit to pay rent to the "lodger" below. Tonight you will see why: it goes where the light is.
shift.4.intro: In your locker: a box of batteries and a note folded in four. "It remembers the smell of people." You do not remember writing that. But it is your handwriting.
shift.5.intro: The main breakers are on the lowest level, where the day crew stopped. Pull all four and the service lift will come down for you. For the first time in five nights the radio is perfectly clear: a voice very like yours, telling you not to come up.
note.1: 9 a.m. Knocking in the west wall, three at a time, then a pause, steady as counting. Strange thing is, it doesn't sound like a threat. It sounds like someone telling us to get away.
note.2: Don't run. It doesn't need to see you. It listens.
note.3: Replaced the level 3 bulbs, fourth time this week. The bulbs aren't blown. Every time, someone has unscrewed them and laid them on the floor in a straight line.
note.4: Loc stood in the dark for an hour and wouldn't answer. When we dragged him out he was ice cold, eyes wide open, staring at the ventilation shaft.
note.5: Mum, down here they set out one extra meal every shift, for someone who isn't on the list. When I asked, the old gatekeeper said: that one's for the lodger.
note.6: Flooding on level 9. Fourteen men. Thirteen recovered. The fourteenth is still clocked in every day.
note.7: IT FOLLOWS SOUND. THROW STONES FAR. DON'T BREATHE LOUD.
note.9:
Phạm Văn Toàn

note.10: If you're reading this, you've been down here five nights already. Go up and you'll have to come back down. Stay, and someone else gets to go up. Follow the knocking at the far west end. Don't be afraid. I was too.
ending.stay:
The cage stands open, its lamp a warm yellow. You turn your back on it.

The knocking in the wall stops. In the tunnel the mass of flesh goes still, its tentacles hanging slack, and for the first time it does not come after you. You lay your hand on the crack. The rock is cold, then warm, then soft as skin.

Somewhere on the surface a man steps out of the lift, thirty years after the day he went down for his shift. In the time book, the name of the fourteenth man is struck through with a shaking pen. Written into the blank line with the red circle is your name.

The next night a small lantern sways its way down into Pit 9. The new worker picks up a scrap of paper, written in a hurry: "Don't run. It listens." The handwriting is yours.

From inside the rock, you knock three times.
tips: Switch the lantern off to hide in the dark, if the rules let darkness help you.
A stone that hits it stuns it for a moment.
Fuse boxes are loud. Be ready to move after you install one.
A burning flare keeps you warm and draws its gaze.
Running feels good until something feels it back.
When it can smell you, hiding does not work. Keep moving and keep your distance.
Glowing eyes mean it is close. Red eyes mean it has found you.
ending:
The cage shudders and slowly begins to climb. Below, something stands in the shaft and watches you go, patient as a landlord seeing a guest to the door.

Up top it is still dark. In the duty room the shift log lies open at a new page. Tomorrow's day crew is already filled in: every name from yesterday's day crew. The last line is yours, written in your own hand.
